changeNote: Owner-authorised bank 4.0.0 revision. Reassessed authority-liberty-03, authority-liberty-07, authority-liberty-08, authority-liberty-11, authority-liberty-12, authority-liberty-15 in the retained subject period; two unchanged-wording claims move within the axis and four claims have new mechanisms. All other 234 answer objects and fourteen other axes are preserved verbatim from revision 4. Retained dossiers, logged source-retrieval passages and specifically recorded supplementary research supply context. New exact responses/intensities are conservatively inferred; this is not a fresh re-verification of every earlier citation or a comprehensive new assessment of later developments. Scoring, weights, axis definitions, images, catalogue exclusions and religion supplements are preserved. No target placement or political-label adjustment is applied.

metadata.name: United Kingdom
metadata.description: UK institutions and implemented policies as at 6 October 2026: parliamentary government, a mixed economy, selective migration routes and cultural accommodation alongside civic integration. This is an institutional assessment, not the opinions of UK residents.
metadata.period: Institutions and implemented policy at 6 October 2026; Labour administration since July 2024
metadata.scope: United Kingdom national institutions and implemented policy, identifying England-only rules and devolved differences. Announced reforms are not treated as completed. Legal recognition is distinguished from public attitudes. Educated assumptions disclose where country-level practice does not settle an exact normative or causal statement.

axes.brief: Competitive elections, opposition and judicial review coexist with Commons confidence, delegated decisions and parliamentary sovereignty. Petition thresholds lead to responses or debate, not citizen-triggered binding law.
axes.counterEvidence: Freedom House reports strong electoral rights but restrictions on protest. Judicial review of executive action is distinct from striking down sovereign primary legislation. Recall has statutory triggers; the UK is not a system of unrestricted public initiation.

axes.brief:
Expression and association are protected, with material restrictions concerning protest, weapons, drugs, surveillance and search. PACE safeguards and warrant exceptions must be read literally.
Focused bank 4.0.0 reassessment: Vaccination-only access competes with alternative certificates and rescinded sector mandates. Reviewed preventive orders, time-limited authorised searches and racial/religious stirring-up offences support bounded controls with different statutory thresholds.
axes.counterEvidence:
Rights reports identify restrictive implementation, not just legal protections. ANPR routine retention is 90 days locally and 12 months nationally; reviewed evidential retention is an exception, not blanket multi-year retention of everyone. Bulk interception requires national-security necessity and oversight.
Focused review: distinguish adult shared-space outbreak conditions from purely personal paternalism, reviewed preventive controls from unreviewed detention, limited threat-area searches from routine suspicionless search, and nonviolent group-hatred incitement from criticism or moral-content censorship. Vaccination-only access competes with alternative certificates and rescinded sector mandates. Reviewed preventive orders, time-limited authorised searches and racial/religious stirring-up offences support bounded controls with different statutory thresholds. Earlier evidence limitations remain; new questions do not establish empirical calibration.

axes.brief: Equality protections, a plural national identity, recognised constituent cultures and religious dress accommodation coexist with English proficiency, shared civic obligations and participation. Private customs are not generally required to be replaced.
axes.counterEvidence: The cohesion document advocates both common identity and pluralism; future programmes are not proof of delivery. Equality duties require consideration of needs, not unlimited spending or a predetermined outcome. Multinational symbolism is only an analogy for the question about Indigenous peoples.

Channel arrivals are not equivalent to permission or asylum refusal; protection claims can succeed following irregular entry. No comprehensive annual settlement quota was identified; proposals are distinguished from commenced rules.
